description:
Work out the EU CBAM certificates owed on imported goods after the free allocation adjustment, what they cost at the official certificate price, and where the importer stands against the 50-tonne annual threshold, on EU default values.
Use when: the user asks what CBAM will cost on cement, fertiliser, iron and steel, aluminium or hydrogen imported into the EU. Instead: uk_cbam_cost for imports into the UK.
Inputs: one line per goods and origin. cn is the CN code (4 to 10 digits); words such as "steel tubes" are matched against the official descriptions and return candidates when several fit. origin is an ISO code or an English country name; tonnes is the net mass. period is 2026-Q1 to 2026-Q4 or a year from 2027, defaulting to the current quarter; 2026 prices are quarterly and later ones weekly, so from 2027 the latest published price applies unless price is sent. other_tonnes adds CBAM goods not listed, for the threshold; unit_kg adds the cost per item.
Behaviour: summary states the result in one sentence. Under 50 t a year (lines plus other_tonnes) owed is none and the totals show what becomes owed above it. A country without its own default values takes the table for other countries and territories, noted in assumed; origins in the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland are refused as outside CBAM. Electricity and verified actual emissions are not covered; an estimate, not a declaration.
Constraints: no authentication, key or headers. At most 10 requests per 10 seconds per IP address; above that HTTP 429, so space out repeated calls.

cn.description: Single line: CN code or words

compare_with.description: Optional second country of origin: the same lines made there, returned as comparison and never added to the totals

lines.description: One item per goods and origin. Or send cn, origin and tonnes for a single line

cn.description: CN code, e.g. "7310" or "73102990", or words describing the goods

origin.description: Country of origin: ISO code such as "CN" or a name such as "Viet Nam"

other_tonnes.description: Other CBAM goods (cement, fertiliser, iron and steel, aluminium) imported this year, tonnes, for the 50 t threshold

path.description: law (default): the free allocation phase-out in force. proposal: COM(2026) 616, not law

period.description: Quarter of import for 2026, e.g. "2026-Q3", or a year from 2027, e.g. "2027". Default: the current quarter

price.description: Certificate price in EUR, to override the published price

tonnes.description: Single line: net mass in tonnes

unit_kg.description: Net mass of one item in kg, e.g. 3.1 for a 20 L steel jerry can, for the cost per item

name: cbam_cost

assumed.description: Each value the tool inferred or defaulted, in words, so it can be checked with the user

candidates.description: When ok is false for words or a heading: the codes to choose from

cite.description: Credit line with a link, for quoting the answer

error.description: When ok is false: what is missing or could not be read, and what to send instead

free_allocation.description: cbam_factor, cscf and path for the year

lines.description: Per line: cn, goods, country, default_table, default_value, mark_up, see_with_mark_up, benchmark, route, embedded_emissions, free_allocation_adjustment, certificates, cost_eur, cost_eur_per_unit_of_quantity, cost_eur_per_item with unit_kg, owed

ok.description: true with an answer. false when the tool needs one more input or cannot answer; error then says what to send

owed.description: all, some (hydrogen only, under the threshold) or none

price_basis.description: Published for the period, given, or the latest published

publisher.description: Who publishes the tool, the Fortitude21 products that fit, with links, and quote_url, a link to ask for a quotation

summary.description: The result in one sentence, threshold included

tool.description: Link to the same answer on the interactive tool page

total.description: certificates and cost_eur for all lines; owed_certificates and owed_cost_eur after the threshold

title: EU CBAM certificates and cost
